title: Confucius3-Math: A Lightweight High-Performance Reasoning LLM for Chinese K-12 Mathematics Learning
extended_summary:
This paper presents Confucius3-Math, an open-source 14B parameter large language model designed specifically for Chinese K-12 mathematics learning and educator support. The paper addresses the problem that many strong general-purpose reasoning models, while good on competition math, do not perform reliably on K-12 educational tasks and may generate incorrect answers that can harm learning. The authors position the work as an effort to build a practical, low-cost reasoning model that is accurate enough for real educational use.

The approach is a post-training reinforcement learning pipeline applied to a selected open-source base model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B), with three technical innovations: Targeted Entropy Regularization, Recent Sample Recovery, and Policy-Specific Hardness Weighting. The system is trained on a mixture of open-source math/reasoning datasets and proprietary Chinese K-12 math questions and solutions, with emphasis on step-by-step explanations and answer correctness. The model is evaluated on internal and public math benchmarks relevant to Chinese K-12 learning, including CK12-MATH, GAOKAO-Bench (Math), MathBench K12, and CMATH, plus competition-level benchmarks such as MATH500 and AIME24/25.

The paper reports that Confucius3-Math outperforms several strong baselines, including DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-14B, and QwQ-32B, on nearly all reported benchmarks, with especially strong gains on the internal Chinese K-12 benchmark. The authors also emphasize practical deployment advantages: the model is lightweight enough to run on consumer-grade hardware, and the training cost is reported as only $26K. Overall, the paper concludes that strong domain-specific reasoning models for K-12 mathematics can be built efficiently with reinforcement learning and carefully curated data.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a technical arXiv model report, not a peer-reviewed educational evaluation, and it does not use a classroom RCT, QED, or student-level causal design. The evidence is benchmark-based model evaluation plus engineering measurements, so it does not meet the credibility criteria for stronger K-12 intervention evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports large gains on math benchmarks and strong efficiency improvements, but these are offline model performance results rather than demonstrated student learning effects. Educational impact is therefore promising but still unclear at the learner-outcome level.

interventions.use_case: A lightweight reasoning LLM trained for Chinese K-12 mathematics learning, intended to answer student math questions and provide problem-solving steps as learning support.

finding.finding_summary: Confucius3-Math achieved the strongest reported accuracy on the paper’s K-12 math benchmarks, including CK12-MATH (96.24%), GAOKAO-Bench Math (98.46%), MathBench K12 (95.10%), and CMATH (96.13%). Against its base model, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, gains were +13.38, +11.71, +6.70, and +18.72 points respectively; on AIME25 it improved by +26.98 points (to 69.95%).
finding.measure: Benchmark accuracy / pass@1 on Chinese K-12 and competition math benchmarks (CK12-MATH, GAOKAO-Bench Math, MathBench K12, CMATH, MATH500, AIME24, AIME25)

finding.finding_summary: The model was designed and evaluated as a low-cost deployment system, with reported inference throughput up to 31,994 tokens/s on H800 hardware and 4,956 output tokens/s on a single RTX 4090D in scaled comparisons. The paper reports a 15.8× throughput advantage over DeepSeek-R1 and a training cost of $26K for 13,109 GPU hours, emphasizing deployment efficiency rather than learner outcomes.
finding.measure: Inference throughput (tokens/s), deployment feasibility, and training cost
